Hi Emma — great to hear and thanks for sending the redline. Looping in Karthik from Legal Ops so we can move quickly.

Quick answers up front:
- We have a Redwood DPA template we typically start with; we can also review your redline and produce a counter if needed.
- We accept both DocuSign and AdobeSign; DocuSign is our default for enterprise, but AdobeSign is okay if that speeds things up.
- I'll attach the current subprocessor export and a simplified data-flow diagram for reference. Our subprocessor roster is updated monthly.
- For EU transfers we rely on the approved EU SCCs (post-2021 standard clauses) and have technical controls and limited access policies documented. If Veridian needs additional safeguards, we can discuss addenda (encryption at rest, contractual access limits).

Action items:
1) Karthik — can you review the attached Veridian redline and propose whether to use the Redwood template or push back on specific clauses? Please flag high-risk clauses (data residency, audit rights, liability caps).
2) Emma — if you prefer DocuSign we'll prepare a DocuSign-ready annex once Karthik confirms the approach.

I'll follow up with an internal counter by EOD Monday (11/23).

Thanks,

On Mon, Nov 23, 2026 at 08:12 Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I'll follow up with an internal counter by EOD Monday (11/23).

Thanks — reviewed Veridian's redline. High-level notes:

- Liability and caps: Veridian has expanded the liability carveouts and removed our carrier sublimit language. We should propose a modest carveout for willful misconduct and keep the commercial cap aligned with the MSA.
- Audit rights & access: Their redline is broad (on-site audits + unlimited access). Recommend offering scoped audit rights (remote review of logs and evidence, with on-site only for material incidents and by mutual agreement).
- Data residency: They request EU-only processing. We can support session-level routing to EU Dedicated for the pilot (subject to procurement approval) — propose a routing addendum rather than a full residency guarantee.
- Subprocessors: we'll provide the current list (attached). For additional subprocessors not on the list, we propose a 10-business-day notice and an objections mechanism.
- E-sign: DocuSign preferred; we will produce a DocuSign-ready annex.

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood produces a short privacy annex (based on our template) that accepts a limited number of Veridian redlines and proposes alternate language for the high-risk clauses.
2) Share the annex in DocuSign with Veridian legal for counters.
3) If Veridian insists on on-site audit or strict EU-only processing we escalate to Security + Sales to assess cost and timeline.

I'll draft the annex and send to Soojin + Laura for sign-off by EOD.

--
Karthik Iyer
Legal Ops Manager | Redwood Inference
